document.name: Temperature Engine Theorem
document.title: Lean 4 Companion — Nawderian Temperature Engine Theorem

purpose.primary: Provide a small formal teaching abstraction for selected algebraic properties associated with the Nawderian Temperature Engine Theorem.
purpose.formal_goal: Represent a signed one-dimensional temperature-force relation and inspect selected zero and sign-change consequences.
purpose.educational_principle: A small algebraic formalization can verify consequences of its definition without validating the broader physical interpretation from which the teaching example was abstracted.

source_alignment.selected_structure: Signed relation between coupling, gradient, and modeled force.

force_relation.alpha: coupling term in the source interpretation
force_relation.gradient_T: directional driver in the source relation

teaching_simplification.purpose: Make selected algebraic consequences directly inspectable.

why_signed_values.purpose: Represent positive, zero, and negative directional values in the teaching model.
why_signed_values.modeling_reason: The sign of the represented gradient and force is part of the property being inspected.
why_signed_values.boundary: Selecting signed integers is a teaching-model choice rather than a claim that the complete physical quantities are naturally integer-valued.

function.name: temperatureForce
function.relationship: negative product of coupling and gradient

formal_targets.name: Zero Gradient Property
formal_targets.meaning: Under the supplied teaching definition, a zero gradient produces zero modeled force.

formal_targets.name: Zero Coupling Property
formal_targets.meaning: Under the supplied teaching definition, zero coupling produces zero modeled force.

formal_targets.name: Gradient Sign-Reversal Property
formal_targets.condition: gradient is replaced by its negation
formal_targets.consequence: the modeled force reverses sign under the supplied relation
formal_targets.meaning: The algebraic model preserves a directional opposition between gradient sign and modeled-force sign.

zero_gradient.reason: The represented product contains a zero factor.
zero_gradient.scope: Algebraic consequence of the teaching definition.

zero_coupling.reason: The represented product contains a zero factor.
zero_coupling.scope: Algebraic consequence of the teaching definition.

sign_reversal.structural_result: The modeled force changes sign under gradient negation according to the represented algebraic relation.
sign_reversal.boundary: This is a statement about the teaching definition, not an experimentally established physical law.

directionality.relation: negative sign between product and modeled output
directionality.educational_question: What changes when the directional input changes sign?

alignment.question: What corresponds?
alignment.formal_answer: The sign and magnitude of the modeled force correspond algebraically to the supplied coupling and gradient under the teaching definition.

coherence.question: Does this hold together?
coherence.formal_answer: The selected zero and sign properties can be checked against the explicit negative-product definition.

clarity.question: Can this be understood and inspected?
clarity.formal_answer: The one-dimensional signed abstraction exposes the selected algebraic relationship while explicitly separating it from broader physical interpretation.

continuity.question: What persists through change?
continuity.formal_answer: The formal relationship remains fixed while coupling or gradient values change, allowing consequence propagation to be inspected.

zero_case_as_clarity.principle: Boundary and zero cases often make the behavior of a definition especially easy to inspect.
zero_case_as_clarity.lesson: Simple formal cases can reveal structural consequences without claiming empirical completeness.

sign_case_as_alignment.principle: Changing sign gives a controlled way to inspect directional correspondence.
sign_case_as_alignment.question: Does the output transform in the way encoded by the relation?

change_one_thing.principle: Vary one formal input at a time when inspecting propagation.
change_one_thing.benefit: Makes it easier to identify which change produced which formal consequence.

future_formalization.rule: Each extension should be justified by the claim being investigated rather than added only to make the model look more physically sophisticated.

vector_extension_boundary.principle: Do not describe the current theorem as though vector calculus were already represented.

units_boundary.principle: A dimensionless teaching abstraction may be useful for algebraic reasoning while remaining insufficient for complete physical interpretation.
